documents.title: DePaul's Approach to Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: Academic Affairs gives no uniform stance: 'Faculty have the discretion to allow or encourage students to use AI' and syllabi 'should make clear' the rules, with general integrity policies as fallback. It treats AI like a person to be cited, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: Short Academic Affairs position statement: AI is treated like a person under existing integrity policies and must be cited; instructors decide course use and must say so in syllabi; the policy is being updated and will evolve.

units.why: The statement of the dual challenge ('prepare our students for a world of work in which AI will certainly play a part') gives a career rationale for engaging with AI. It states a rationale, not a rule, so it is informs/neutral of type P44.
units.anchor: prepare our students for a world of work in which AI will certainly
units.resolution_why: Coders differed only on actor (A: all, B: admin). The sentence is a rationale that binds nobody, so actor is all; the university-as-actor reading is reserved for the 'responsibility to create conditions' unit.

units.why: Balances the career rationale with integrity: students should 'understand and practice integrity in the use of any sources, including those generated by Artificial Intelligence'. It is a principle that frames the institution's approach, so P56 (framework/principles) fits better than P45, which needs an explicit collaborator analogy.
units.anchor: understand and practice integrity in the use of any sources
units.resolution_why: Coders differed only on actor (A: all, B: admin). The sentence states what the university wants for students and binds no office, so all.

units.why: 'Used irresponsibly, it can spread misinformation' names a harm of AI; it is informational (informs) and fits P53 on harms.
units.anchor: Used irresponsibly, it can spread misinformation
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this unit. The source says 'Used irresponsibly, it can spread misinformation', a stated harm of AI. It is a real, if brief, statement of concern, so it is kept as P53 informs/neutral.

units.why: The university states 'a responsibility to create conditions' for the community to learn about benefits and dangers of AI and act responsibly; this is an institution-level statement of purpose, so P56 and admin as actor.
units.anchor: responsibility to create conditions for members of the University community to learn

units.why: Academic Affairs commits to Teaching Commons materials 'for faculty on best practices in incorporating AI into courses where appropriate, and preventing its use where that approach is necessary'; this is faculty support (P63), not a stance rule.
units.anchor: a growing body of materials for faculty on best practices in incorporating AI into courses

units.why: 'AI can be considered analogous to a person, and our relevant policies apply' treats AI like a human collaborator or outside source under existing rules, which is exactly P45.
units.anchor: AI can be considered analogous to a person, and our relevant policies apply

units.why: States that AI-generated content 'is a "source" and should be cited appropriately'; this is a disclosure/citation duty for students (P24), modality should.
units.anchor: content generated by AI is a "source" and should be cited appropriately

units.why: The policy is being updated so AI is a source that "cannot stand in for the student's own work". It forbids AI substituting for the student's work (P19), a must-not for students; the update itself is coded separately.
units.anchor: cannot stand in for the student’s own work
units.frag_start: the policy is in the process of being updated
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase (A: general, B: during-work). The source says AI content 'cannot stand in for the student's own work', a rule about the work students produce and submit, so during-work. Both agree on P19 must-not, student.

units.why: The policy is 'in the process of being updated to include AI'; a statement that the integrity policy is provisional and being revised, so P54.
units.anchor: the policy is in the process of being updated to include AI
units.frag_start: the policy is in the process

units.why: Applies the Research Misconduct policy's plagiarism definition to AI: 'it is reasonable to consider AI as analogous to "another person"'. This is the same analogy as the coursework unit, treating AI as an outside source under existing rules (P45). P62 would need an AI rule specific to research or scholarship, and the passage sets none.
units.anchor: it is reasonable to consider AI as analogous to
units.frag_start: and it is reasonable to consider AI
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type (A: P62, B: P45). The source extends an existing definition of plagiarism to AI by analogy and states no research-specific AI rule, so P45 (treat AI like another person under existing rules) fits and P62 does not.

units.why: 'Faculty have the discretion to allow or encourage students to use AI' puts the decision with individual instructors, so P04 with modality may.
units.anchor: Faculty have the discretion to allow or encourage students to use AI

units.why: 'Course syllabi should make clear how students may or may not use AI' asks for an AI statement in syllabi, which is P09.
units.anchor: Course syllabi should make clear how students may or may not use AI

units.why: 'In the absence of a course-specific AI policy, the general Academic Integrity and Research Misconduct policies apply' is the fallback when a syllabus is silent (P06).
units.anchor: In the absence of a course-specific AI policy, the general

units.why: 'When in doubt, cite the AI source like any other' tells students to cite AI in cases of uncertainty; it is chiefly a citation duty (P24), not an instruction to ask the instructor (P10).
units.anchor: When in doubt, cite the AI source like any other.

units.why: "Conventions for its proper use will likely evolve over time": the approach is acknowledged as provisional, so P54.
units.anchor: conventions for its proper use will likely evolve over time
units.frag_start: As Artificial Intelligence becomes more widespread, conventions
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on actor (A: all, B: admin). The sentence is the institution acknowledging that conventions will change, in line with the other P54 units, so admin.

units.why: Invites suggestions and expertise via a named contact and says the Center for Teaching and Learning 'will help route your feedback'; feedback is invited, so P54.
units.anchor: If you have suggestions, can provide expertise, and want to engage actively
units.frag_end: connect you to collaborators, stakeholders, and resources.

documents.title: Teaching Guides: Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The guide sets no rule on student AI use; it defines AI, offers recommendations ('Draft a syllabus statement') and resources and leaves rules to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: Teaching Commons guide: defines AI, notes the free Copilot, FERPA data cautions, steps for instructors, assignment ideas, and an AI detector page. It sets no student-use rule.

units.why: Defines AI and generative AI ('tools that source existing data to create new artifacts in response to user prompts'), setting what the guide covers: P61.
units.anchor: Generative artificial intelligence refers to a suite of tools that source existing data

units.why: States that faculty, staff and students can use Microsoft Copilot 'using their DePaul credentials'; this is an institution-provided AI tool, so P17.
units.anchor: DePaul faculty, staff, and students can

units.why: The Guiding Principles line says 'we're encouraged to learn more about emerging AI technologies and help students to learn to use them responsibly'. It is an institution-level principle encouraging learning about AI and sets no use rule, so P56 with should/encourage.
units.anchor: encouraged to learn more about emerging AI technologies and help students to learn
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type (A: P56, B: P44). The line sits under 'DePaul's Guiding Principles' and is a preamble-level principle; P44 needs a course-level practice of teaching or demonstrating AI use, which the line does not state. P56 chosen.

units.why: Quotes the principle that 'Catholic Vincentian values guide our use of all technology, including AI'; a values-based preamble, so P56.
units.anchor: Catholic Vincentian values guide our use of all technology, including AI
units.frag_end: spiritual well-being of our diverse local and global communities."

units.why: 'FERPA-protected data cannot be shared to a third-party service — including AI platforms — without student consent' restricts sharing student data with AI tools: personal data protection (P50).
units.anchor: FERPA-protected data cannot be shared to a third-party service
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on actor (A: all, B: instructor). The sentence states a general FERPA rule for any party sharing student data and names no addressee, so all.

units.why: Says Copilot with BlueKey 'has these institutional agreements in place and is FERPA compliant', pointing to a vetted tool for protected data: P50 (prefer vetted tools).
units.anchor: DePaul's Copilot with BlueKey AI service has these institutional agreements in place
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on actor (A: all, B: instructor). The passage names no addressee, so all, as for the preceding FERPA unit.

units.why: 'It is still a best practice to avoid using personally identifiable information whenever possible' is advice to protect personal data: P50.
units.anchor: best practice to avoid using personally identifiable information whenever possible
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on actor (A: all, B: instructor). The passage names no addressee, so all, as for the FERPA units.

units.why: Step one for instructors is to 'Draft a syllabus statement and discuss academic integrity with students', asking for an AI statement in the syllabus, which is P09. Drafting the statement is course design, so before-course; no specific stance is prescribed.
units.anchor: Draft a syllabus statement and discuss academic integrity with students.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase (A: before-course, B: course-start). The verb is 'draft', preparing the statement, so before-course; both agree on P09 should, instructor.

units.why: "Look for opportunities to check in with students' processes and learning strategies" advises process check-ins. No type covers process check-ins as such (P34 is code reviews or oral exams to verify understanding; P35 is assignment redesign), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Look for opportunities to check in with students’ processes and learning strategies.
units.frag_start: Look for opportunities to check in
units.uncovered_note: Instructors are advised to check in on students' processes and learning strategies as an AI-era teaching practice; not verification of understanding or assignment redesign.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type (A: P35, B: UNCOVERED). The source only advises checking in on students' 'processes and learning strategies'. P35 covers redesigned assignments and grading around process, P34 covers meetings where students explain their work; the check-in is neither, so UNCOVERED.

units.why: 'Use your assignment prompts to experiment with generative AI tools' asks instructors to try AI on their own assignments, which is faculty learning (P63).
units.anchor: Use your assignment prompts to experiment with generative AI tools.

units.why: 'Discuss the possibilities and limitations of generative AI tools with students' asks instructors to teach about AI in class (P44), also touching limits of tools.
units.anchor: Discuss the possibilities and limitations of generative AI tools with students.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance (A: encourage, B: neutral). The line asks instructors to discuss possibilities and limits of AI, which neither encourages nor restricts student use, so neutral. Both agree on P44.

units.why: Points instructors to assignments 'curated by DePaul faculty and Center for Teaching and Learning staff' using different tools; support for faculty adopting AI (P63).
units.anchor: curated by DePaul faculty and Center for Teaching and Learning staff
units.frag_start: list of additional generative AI assignments
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type (A: P63, B: P44), actor (A: admin, B: instructor) and stance. The sentence points instructors to assignment lists curated by CTL staff and faculty, a resource for faculty and not a rule that courses teach AI use, so P63, admin as provider, informs/neutral.

units.why: The AI Detectors section 'explores the capabilities and limitations of AI detection tools' and offers recommendations. It does not say detectors are unreliable or used, so it is faculty support (P63) rather than P39 or P40.
units.anchor: explores the capabilities and limitations of AI detection tools
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type (A: P63, B: UNCOVERED) and actor (A: admin, B: instructor). The AI Detectors section is a teaching-center resource on capabilities and limits of detectors, fitting faculty support (P63); it states no position, so neither P39 nor P40. Actor is admin as the provider.

units.why: Lists newsletters, Google group and other resources "for engaging with higher education's ongoing responses to generative AI", which supports instructors in learning about AI (P63).
units.anchor: great resources for engaging with higher education’s ongoing responses to generative AI
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this unit. The source calls newsletters, groups and blogs 'great resources for engaging with higher education's ongoing responses to generative AI', a recommendation to instructors to stay current, so P63. B's separate 'Events' and 'suggest additions' lines are navigation and are dropped.

documents.title: Generative AI (Information Services)
documents.stance_why: The page restricts AI use by default: autonomous agents are 'strictly prohibited' without approval, most university data may not go to an LLM except Copilot Chat, and students are told 'Never use AI tools without direct guidance and approval from instructors'. That is ban unless permitted, so restrict.
documents.summary: Information Services guidance on data protection and tools: Copilot Chat is the approved tool for public and internal data, other LLMs are barred for protected data, autonomous agents need approval, shared AI-built apps need review, and students need instructor approval.

units.why: Defines AI and generative AI ('technology that enables computers to perform portions of tasks that typically require human intelligence'): P61.
units.anchor: Artificial intelligence (AI) refers to technology that enables computers to perform portions of tasks

units.why: 'Most university data should never be uploaded or used with an LLM or AI-based tool' forbids uploading university data to AI tools; the concern is data protection (P50), not course materials (P49).
units.anchor: Most university data should never be uploaded or used with an LLM or AI-based tool.

units.why: Directs readers to the Data Security Classifications Standard and AI Guidelines for how policy applies to AI, an instruction to follow the data-protection standards (P50).
units.anchor: Data Security Classifications and Controls Standard
units.frag_start: Please review the Data Security Classifications
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this unit. 'Please review the Data Security Classifications and Controls Standard' is a directive to consult the data-protection standard before using AI, so kept as P50 should.

units.why: Any AI-based app or service that 'interacts with any other members of the DePaul community' must 'undergo a thorough design, security, and data review'. No type covers review of AI-built services, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: this service must undergo a thorough design, security, and data review
units.uncovered_note: Required design, security and data review before an AI-based app or service is offered to other members of the university community.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase (A: general, B: before-course). The sentence applies to anyone building a service at any time, so general.

units.why: 'The use of autonomous agents is strictly prohibited at DePaul without the express approval of Information Services' bans agents by default, matching P07 (autonomous coding agents).
units.anchor: The use of autonomous agents is strictly prohibited at DePaul without the express approval

units.why: "Autonomous agents like OpenClaw or Claude Cowork are explicitly prohibited even if they are only accessing your 'own' account": a named, categorical agent ban, P07.
units.anchor: autonomous agents like OpenClaw or Claude Cowork are explicitly prohibited
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this unit. It adds that named agents (OpenClaw, Claude Cowork) are prohibited even on the user's own account, which narrows the earlier agent rule, so kept as a separate P07 must-not.

units.why: 'Some AI tools can be employed for personal use with great caution. Others shouldn't ever be used by DePaul community members' opens the guiding principles by sorting tools into cautioned and forbidden. It states a principle with no data content, so P56, should-not, restrict.
units.anchor: Some AI tools can be employed for personal use with great caution.
units.frag_start: Some AI tools can be employed
units.frag_end: shouldn’t ever be used by DePaul community members.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this unit (as P50 informs). The sentence names no data and states a principle that some tools should never be used, so kept as P56 should-not/restrict.

units.why: 'Don't provide any sensitive, highly sensitive, or internal restricted DePaul data ... to any LLM platform' names ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude as disallowed with non-public data: P50.
units.anchor: Don’t provide any sensitive, highly sensitive, or internal restricted DePaul data

units.why: 'When in doubt, avoid supplying DePaul data to any LLM platform that isn't Copilot Chat' prefers the vetted tool when unsure (P50).
units.anchor: When in doubt, avoid supplying DePaul data to any LLM platform that isn’t Copilot Chat

units.why: 'Copilot Chat is the approved general purpose LLM platform at DePaul' with a Microsoft contract keeping data private: a sanctioned university tool (P17).
units.anchor: Copilot Chat is the approved general purpose LLM platform at DePaul.

units.why: Even with Copilot Chat, 'you should only use data categorized as public and internal non-restricted'; a limit on data protection with the vetted tool: P50.
units.anchor: you should only use data categorized as public and internal non-restricted

units.why: Tells units' members to 'Check with your area' about pre-approved AI tools, which are security-reviewed tools provided by schools or offices: P17.
units.anchor: may already have access to powerful AI tools that have undergone security review
units.frag_end: usage guidelines for these pre-approved tools.

units.why: Vibe-coding or app-building is allowed 'for professional use if they are strictly used by the individual and not shared', with sharing requiring review. It is a conditional permission on AI-built apps that fits no coursework type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: build apps or tools for professional use if they are strictly used by the individual
units.uncovered_note: Conditional permission to build apps with AI/vibe-coding tools when used only individually, with no protected data, and not shared.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type (A: UNCOVERED, B: P07). The passage allows building apps with 'vibe-coding' tools for individual professional use if no protected data is used. P07 covers AI in editors, IDEs and coding agents; this is a conditional permission on app-building, which fits no type, so UNCOVERED.

units.why: 'Once an app or tool is shared with others, it requires a thorough review like any other technology application' extends the review requirement to shared AI-built apps. No type covers review of AI-built tools (P65 is vendor agreements), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Once an app or tool is shared with others, it requires a thorough review
units.frag_start: Once an app or tool is shared
units.uncovered_note: AI-built apps or tools shared with others require a thorough review like any other university technology service.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this unit as separate. The source states a distinct trigger (sharing an AI-built app), so kept as UNCOVERED, same note as the other review unit.

units.why: 'the use of university tools to generate personal profit is prohibited' and AI-built apps must not appear university-endorsed; a restriction on AI-built tools, not a type in the list, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: the use of university tools to generate personal profit is prohibited
units.uncovered_note: AI-built apps must not appear created or endorsed by the university, and university tools may not be used for personal profit.

units.why: Says AI services are 'largely similar to any other software or technology service when it comes to data privacy and security', so existing policies apply, and points to AI Guidelines. A framework-level scope statement (P56).
units.anchor: largely similar to any other software or technology service when it comes to data privacy
units.frag_end: Guidelines to understand how existing university policies apply

units.why: "The critical importance of data protection, security considerations, and responsible use of technology must be central" to any AI endeavor: principle statement, P56.
units.anchor: responsible use of technology must be central to any new endeavor that utilizes artificial intelligence
units.frag_start: the critical importance of data protection, security considerations,
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this unit. 'The critical importance of data protection, security considerations, and responsible use of technology must be central' is a principle for any AI endeavor, so kept as P56.

units.why: 'all DePaul students, faculty, and staff are encouraged to consult with your schools, departments, instructors, or managers' and be transparent so that use is approved: ask before using (P10).
units.anchor: encouraged to consult with your schools, departments, instructors, or managers
units.frag_start: Before using any AI tools, all
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase (A: general, B: course-start). The consult-and-be-transparent request is for students, faculty and staff in all settings, so general.

units.why: Students are 'encouraged to review course materials for each class and follow the guidance of their instructors', handing the course rule to the instructor (P04).
units.anchor: review course materials for each class and follow the guidance of their instructors

units.why: 'Never use AI tools without direct guidance and approval from instructors and school administrators' is a default ban unless approved, i.e. the fallback rule (P06).
units.anchor: Never use AI tools without direct guidance and approval from instructors and school administrators.

units.why: 'DePaul faculty members are encouraged to learn more about AI in the classrooms' through the Teaching Commons and the Provost's Advisory Committee, so support for faculty learning: P63.
units.anchor: encouraged to learn more about AI in the classrooms
units.frag_end: Center for Teaching & Learning about AI tools in the classroom.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance (A: encourage, B: neutral). The line encourages faculty to learn about AI, which is support and takes no position on AI use, so neutral.

notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. Three university-layer documents; no school, computing or course documents collected. Dropped as non-policy: B's 'It can also generate basic code' (tool description), B's Events/suggest-additions lines (navigation) and B's 'important university safeguards' lead-in (vacuous). The three AI-built-app units on the Information Services page are UNCOVERED and may warrant a new type.
